task: Make trusted release-unit execution resumable when an earlier attempt already pushed the exact child materialization branch but failed before PR/state persistence, reusing only a provably equivalent remote materialization and failing closed on drift.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Trusted executor rerun 37566854069 / job 112621423551 encountered an already-existing canonical U01 branch from the previous attempt, regenerated the same logical materialization as a different commit SHA, and blindly pushed it. Git rejected the non-fast-forward update before child PR creation, proving the executor is not resumable across the materialization-to-PR persistence gap.
observableOutcomes: If the release-unit branch does not exist, the executor pushes the prepared materialization normally.

If the branch exists and its sole parent equals targetBaseSha, tree equals the newly prepared tree, and canonical release-unit commit message identity matches, the executor reuses the existing remote head without pushing.
If any existing remote branch base, tree, or canonical identity differs, execution fails closed and does not force-push or create a PR.
The reused remote head becomes the persisted materialization/PR head so subsequent exact CI proof remains bound to the actually existing branch commit.
unresolvedRisks: A stale or operator-modified remote branch must never be silently accepted.
Remote branch movement between discovery and fetch must block.
Reuse must not weaken child PR exact-head, manifest, binding, CAS, Truth or Lifecycle checks.

in: Add exact remote materialization reconciliation to scripts/release-unit-github-runtime.mjs.
Reuse an existing equivalent remote branch head on rerun and preserve fail-closed drift checks.
Add regression proof for exact reuse without push and tree-drift blocking.
out: No force push of release-unit branches.
No manual child PR creation or state fabrication.
No changes to release decomposition, Release Risk, Atlas, Completion Truth, Lifecycle, storefront, database or product runtime.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This code holds write authority in the trusted release executor and must safely distinguish resumable equivalent state from branch drift.

acceptanceCriteria: Exact pre-existing U01 remote materialization is reused without git push and returned as materializedHeadSha.
Different remote tree blocks with RELEASE_UNIT_REMOTE_BRANCH_TREE_DRIFT.
Different base or canonical identity also blocks before PR creation.
Exact-head CI passes all canonical guards and Completion Truth/Lifecycle before merge.
After merge, rerunning the original rehearsal advances canonically from the persisted CAS state and existing U01 branch.
invariants: Existing remote state is authoritative only after exact base+tree+identity proof.
Child PR validation still binds exact head, base and binding digest.
Parent CAS state and source commit identity remain unchanged.

failureModes: Previous attempt pushed branch but failed before state persisted.
Rerun creates same tree/message with a different commit timestamp SHA.
Remote branch was modified and no longer represents the prepared unit.
Remote branch moves between ls-remote and fetch.
edgeCases: Exact remote branch exists with different SHA but equivalent tree/message/base.
Remote branch has same tree but wrong manifest/binding message.

alternatives.summary: Reconcile and reuse existing remote materialization only after exact base/tree/identity proof.
alternatives.reason: Makes rerun resumable without weakening branch integrity.

alternatives.summary: Force-push newly generated materialization over existing branch.
alternatives.reason: Would destroy prior execution evidence and weaken fail-closed semantics.

alternatives.summary: Manually create the child PR from the existing branch.
alternatives.reason: Would bypass canonical trusted executor orchestration and invalidate the rehearsal.

specialistReviews.finding: The failure is a missing resume edge between remote materialization and persisted PR state.
specialistReviews.resolution: Reconcile existing branch before state transition using base/tree/canonical identity.

specialistReviews.finding: Accepting an existing branch by name alone would allow stale or modified code into trusted execution.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require exact sole parent, exact tree, exact canonical commit message and stable fetched head; otherwise block.

specialistReviews.finding: Normal push is correct only when the release-unit branch is absent.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve normal push on absence and reuse exact remote head on equivalent pre-existence.

specialistReviews.finding: Live rehearsal exposed non-idempotent materialization recovery after an earlier PR-policy failure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Lock both reuse and drift-block semantics with regression tests.

challenge.scenario: Existing branch points to arbitrary code with the expected branch name.
challenge.resolution: Require exact base/tree/canonical message before reuse.

challenge.scenario: Equivalent materialization is regenerated with a different commit SHA because commit metadata differs.
challenge.finding: SHA equality is too strict for recovery when the tree and canonical identity are identical.
challenge.resolution: Compare base, tree and canonical message; reuse the existing remote SHA as the execution head.

challenge.finding: A TOCTOU race could validate one head but use another.
challenge.resolution: Fetch the branch and require FETCH_HEAD to equal the discovered remote SHA.

challenge.scenario: Existing branch has same tree but wrong release-unit manifest/binding identity.
challenge.finding: Tree equality alone does not prove transaction identity.
challenge.resolution: Require exact canonical release-unit commit message generated from the sealed manifest.

challenge.finding: Recovery logic must not change first-attempt semantics.
challenge.resolution: Use existing normal pushExactMaterializedCommit path unchanged.

challenge.scenario: Existing remote branch has the expected tree and message but two parents.
challenge.finding: A merge-shaped child commit would not represent the canonical single-base materialization.
challenge.resolution: Require exactly one parent and require that sole parent to equal targetBaseSha.

challenge.scenario: The existing branch is exact but the local prepared receipt belongs to another manifest or binding.
challenge.finding: Remote validation must not paper over a local transaction identity mismatch.
challenge.resolution: Require receipt target base, manifest digest and binding digest to match the sealed manifest before any remote reuse check.

challenge.scenario: The prior attempt pushed exact U01 but state remained PLANNED because failure happened before persistence.
challenge.finding: Recovery must reconstruct the MATERIALIZED/PR_OPEN state from verifiable repository reality rather than fabricate state.
challenge.resolution: Reuse the exact remote head, then pass it through the existing MATERIALIZED and PR_OPEN event functions and CAS persistence path.

proofPlan: Run exact-head Plan Before Code with active plan covering runtime and regression test.
Require Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, full tests, typecheck and build PASS.
Require Completion Truth VERIFIED and normal Lifecycle closure.
Merge exact fix head to main and verify fresh main CI.
Rerun the original trusted executor from the unchanged rehearsal source and persisted CAS state; accept only canonical child PR/state progression.

requirements.requirement: Trusted release-unit execution must resume across an already-pushed exact child materialization without destructive push or manual bypass, and must block on incompatible remote state.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Rerun may not blindly push a regenerated commit over an existing release-unit branch.
Existing remote materialization may not be reused unless base, tree and canonical identity match.

notes: Created from live rehearsal Failure Intake #988 after trusted executor rerun job 112621423551 proved a missing resumability edge: U01 branch af0365ec... already existed, but the driver generated fb11f556... and attempted a non-fast-forward push. Fix is deliberately narrow: exact remote reuse after base/tree/message proof, otherwise fail closed.
